items.summary: "Vete Ya," "Cómo Me Duele" and other iconic tracks that defined Elizalde's legacy as "El Gallo de Oro."
items.body: This Wednesday (Nov. 25) marks 20 years since the assassination of Valentín Elizalde , the regional Mexican singer who, at the height of his career, was gunned down after a performance in Reynosa, in northern Mexico, along with his manager Mario Mendoza and his driver Reynaldo Ballesteros. To this day, the reasons or culprits behind the crime remain unknown. At just 27 years old, the singer from Sonora was already an icon, thanks to his commanding personality and unique interpretive style, accompanied by Sinaloan banda music. Despite not possessing a powerful voice, Elizalde poured emotion into songs like “Vete Ya,” “Cómo Me Duele,” “Vencedor” and “Te Quiero Así,” which have become timeless classics in Mexican music. The Live Nation-promoted tour will bring the group to stadiums beginning on Aug. 13 with a show at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, Fla., followed by stops in Atlanta, Baltimore, East Rutherford, N.J., Chicago and Toronto before winding down on Sept. 14 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass.; those shows will feature support from Stephen Wilson Jr. The dates will pick up again on Sept. 27 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, followed by a double-down at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles (Oct. 1-2) and stops in Las Vegas and Santa Clara, Calif. before wrapping things up on Oct. 18 at BC Place in Vancouver; the War on Drugs will support on the second run of North American shows. items.title: Rauw Alejandro Is Fulfilling a Childhood Dream With Rockstar Games: ”GTA’ Has Been Part of My Life’
items.summary: Alejandro chats with Billboard about joining the GTA VI soundtrack and bringing throwback reggaetón energy to the game with “Macacoa 2000.”
items.body: Like many adults right now, Rauw Alejandro is probably glued to the couch playing Grand Theft Auto VI . Age is nothing but a number for millennials who grew up reveling in the criminal escapades and explosive gameplay Rockstar Games has offered gamers over the last two decades. Now, Rauw isn’t just reliving his childhood; he’s part of one of the biggest video games in history, thanks to his inclusion on the blockbuster soundtrack, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album . “When I heard about the opportunity, I was like, ‘Let’s gooo! We gotta bring that Puerto Rican underground sound to GTA y más que nuevamente regresa a Miami , home of many Latinos,’” he tells Billboard . “Growing up playing GTA , I never imagined I’d get to be part of its soundtrack. As a fan, it’s crazy to experience something like this. GTA has always been about the culture, and now getting to bring my own sound into that world is just insane. It’s a full-circle moment for me, de verdad . Something really special.” Alejandro’s electric track, “Macacoa 2000,” is a love letter to throwback reggaeton that complements the game’s Miami-inspired setting. items.title: HONOR’s first wide foldable is tipped for a March 2027 launch with a seamless new hinge
items.summary: HONOR’s answer to the iPhone Duo and the Z Fold 8 comes next year.
items.body: TL;DR HONOR’s first wide foldable phone is tipped to launch around March 2027 with a 7.6-inch inner display and a hinge that minimizes the appearance of the crease. The device is expected to feature a flagship 2nm Snapdragon chipset, a 200MP main camera, and a periscope telephoto lens. The foldable could pack a class-leading 7,000mAh battery and retail for around $1,500 in China. We’ve known for a while now that HONOR is working on a widescreen competitor to the likes of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the iPhone Duo , and now we know that the device could finally make its way to interested buyers around March 2027. The new detail comes courtesy of Digital Chat Station on Weibo, who has previously shared several key specs related to HONOR’s potentially upcoming wide foldable. What the tipster hasn’t shared before, however, is that the Shenzhen, China-based company might be putting a lot of effort into eliminating the upcoming foldable’s crease.

items.title: Almost Monday Scores Second Alternative Airplay No. 1 With ‘No More Regrets’
items.summary: The trio first topped the chart in 2025 with “Can’t Slow Down.”
items.body: Almost Monday earns its second No. 1 hit on Billboard ’s Alternative Airplay chart (dated Nov. 28) with “No More Regrets.” The song, released May 1 via Hollywood Records, rises two places to the summit thanks to a 5% increase in spins at the format Nov. 13-19, according to Luminate. (The Alternative Airplay chart measures songs’ weekly plays, as tabulated by Mediabase and provided to Billboard by Luminate, on 60 U.S. alternative radio stations.) The San Diego-based trio first led Alternative Airplay in February 2025 with “Can’t Slow Down,” a crossover hit that also reached No. 12 on Adult Pop Airplay and No. 24 on Pop Airplay. “No More Regrets” is Almost Monday’s eighth career Alternative Airplay entry. The group first made the ranking in October 2020 with “Broken People,” which reached No. 26. Earlier this year, “Lost” hit No. 18. The coronation is also a milestone for Hollywood Records, which earns its third Alternative Airplay No. 1. items.body: Credit: HUAWEI TL;DR HUAWEI has launched its Watch Air, which is thinner than most modern smartwatches. The Watch Air is only 6.9mm thick and weighs just 29 grams. It runs HarmonyOS 2.0 and works with both Android and iOS. HUAWEI might have been forced to stop selling its devices in the US, along with most of the world, but that hasn’t stopped it from pushing the limits of innovation. Earlier today, the company announced its latest foldable, the Mate X8 , with an eye-searingly bright display and a promise that the hinge will last 700,000 folds. The phone even uses levitating magnets under the screen to reduce strain on the folding screen and limit creasing. Another selling point of the Mate X8 is that it’s the slimmest foldable on the market, measuring just 4.2mm when unfolded. To complement the sleek foldable, HUAWEI has also announced a smartwatch significantly slimmer than the latest Pixel or Galaxy Watch devices. Called the HUAWEI Watch Air, the smartwatch measures only 6.9mm in thickness, excluding the sensor area, and weighs just 27 grams. items.title: YouTube Music could finally let you pin your favorite playlists and albums where they belong
items.summary: Spotify users have enjoyed library pinning for a while, and it looks like YouTube Music is finally catching up.
items.body: TL;DR YouTube Music is working on a new feature that could let users pin songs, albums, playlists, and artists directly to their Library for quicker access. The feature is separate from the existing Pin to Speed dial option, which only adds shortcuts to the Home tab. Spotify already offers Library pinning, but it’s unclear how Google’s implementation will work or when it will roll out. YouTube Music might finally be addressing one of those little annoyances that can make using a music streaming app more frustrating than it needs to be — having to hunt through your Library to find the music you listen to the most. We’ve spotted signs of a new pinning feature in the latest YouTube Music Android app (version 9.46.55), and it could let users pin their favorite songs, albums, and playlists directly to the Library tab, making frequently played music much easier to find.

items.title: HUAWEI’s first continuous glucose monitor is here, costs just under $50
items.summary: Expect a MARD value of 7.06%, up to 16 days of use, and (unfortunately) a China-only release.
items.body: Credit: HUAWEI TL;DR HUAWEI has launched the Sense G1 continuous glucose monitor in China. The device lets users view their glucose levels via a connected phone or wearable and offers updates every minute. The Sense G1 costs ~$45 in its home market, but we hope it eventually releases outside China. HUAWEI confirmed earlier this month that it would launch its first continuous glucose monitor (CGM) , dubbed the Sense G1. We didn’t get pricing and availability details back then, but the firm has now launched the device in China. The Sense G1 CGM is the firm’s first Class III medical device and allows users to view their glucose levels via a connected phone or wearable. In fact, you can view your levels on a HUAWEI watch by simply raising your wrist. HUAWEI explains that the CGM offers updates every minute and has a warm-up time of 30 minutes. You can also get alerts for abnormal blood sugar levels, such as high/low levels and emergency low blood sugar. As for measurement accuracy, the manufacturer promises a Mean Absolute Releative Difference (MARD) value of 7.06%.

items.title: Samsung’s Tizen-based Galaxy Watch gets an unofficial Wear OS 3.5 port
items.summary: Eight years later, there's potentially more life in this old watch.
items.body: TL;DR A developer has released an unofficial Wear OS 3.5 port based on Android 11 for the original Samsung Galaxy Watch (SM-R800). The port uses Pixel Watch software and reportedly supports Gemini, the Play Store, GPS, and health tracking. The port and installation guide are available on GitHub, though it remains experimental. Samsung’s switch from Tizen to Wear OS in 2021 opened up a whole new world of apps and Google services for Galaxy Watch owners. But you needed a Galaxy Watch 4 or newer to enjoy those benefits. Older models were left behind, and as Samsung wound down its Tizen smartwatch ecosystem , their usefulness gradually diminished. However, one developer is giving the original Galaxy Watch another shot at life. A developer known as Depth118 has shared an unofficial Android 11-based Wear OS 3.5 port on GitHub for Samsung’s 2018 Galaxy Watch. The project uses software from the original Google Pixel Watch, which, despite launching four years later, shares the same Exynos 9110 processor. The port is specifically designed for the 46mm Bluetooth Galaxy Watch (SM-R800), and the list of features the developer claims to have working is surprisingly extensive.

items.title: The best Android keyboard app isn’t on the Play Store. Here’s how to install it
items.summary: HeliBoard brings customization, clipboard history and offline typing to Android, without Google’s data collection.
items.body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority Android’s always been the go-to destination when it comes to customisation and dialing in the experience exactly as you want it, and that extends to switching out the keyboard for something a bit more bespoke. For the longest time, finding a good keyboard for Android usually meant choosing between Gboard and SwiftKey . Both are excellent at predicting what you’re going to type, correcting spelling mistakes and letting you swipe between letters. The catch is that both these keyboards are made by mega corps, Google and Microsoft, and data collection is part and parcel of the deal. That’s why I’ve been looking at HeliBoard. It’s a free, open-source keyboard that offers many of the same features you’d expect from a modern Android keyboard without needing an internet connection, and, most importantly, no data collection. There are no advertisements, no cloud-based processing and plenty of customization options as is to be expected with open-source apps. There’s just one catch, you won’t find the app on the Google Play Store.

Users could describe their preferred accent, tone, speaking speed, and other vocal characteristics instead of choosing from preset voices. The feature could also include a “Surprise me” option for discovering new voices without writing a prompt. For all the progress we’ve made with voice assistants over the years, personalizing how they sound still feels a little like picking a ringtone in the early 2000s. You’re given a list of options, listen to a few, and settle for whichever sounds closest to what you want. Even with Google adding 66 new regional voices to Gemini just last week, that’s essentially how things work today. items.title: YouTube introduces a new mute button on mobile, but not everyone is happy
items.summary: Users keep pressing by accident.
items.body: TL;DR YouTube is rolling out a dedicated mute button within its mobile video player, letting users silence videos without adjusting their device’s volume. Some users are frustrated by the button’s placement, reporting accidental presses when trying to skip forward in videos. The feature appears to be rolling out gradually. We have it on iOS, but not on Android. YouTube is finally giving users on its mobile apps an easier way to outright silence video without having to fiddle with their device’s volume controls, and it’s manifesting in the form of a dedicated mute button . Although the new button does sound like a welcome addition, many users are already finding the change frustrating , mainly because of accidental presses. The quality-of-life change doesn’t appear to be entirely new. We found a Reddit post from early October highlighting the mute button, suggesting that the streaming giant has been experimenting with it since then, at the very least. However, more recent reports indicate that the button is now making its way to a lot more users simultaneously (thanks @GreenShades9 ).

Amazon previously discontinued Kindle Store support for devices released in 2012 or earlier, but there’s no confirmed cutoff date for these newer models. One of the best things about owning a Kindle is that you don’t have to replace it every few years. As long as the screen works and the battery holds up, even an older model can serve you well. Unfortunately, if you’re still using a 10th-generation Kindle or Kindle Paperwhite, there’s some disappointing news. As first spotted by Good e-Reader , Amazon is ending software support for both e-readers . The 10th-generation Kindle, released in April 2019, and the Kindle Paperwhite, which arrived in November 2018, will no longer receive software updates, including security patches.
